quarterly_data.signal: CFO Deb McCann: Q2 revenue was $474 million, down 2% year over year or -5.2% in constant currency, primarily on the timing of ClearPath software license renewals, and about $20 million above the prior outlook - fully from Technology Solutions & Services (TS&S, the company excluding ClearPath), whose revenue of $404 million rose 2% (a 1.3% decline in constant currency). CEO Mike Thomson: revenue up across key solutions and applications, cybersecurity and data center field services.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $474 million (-2%; -5.2% constant currency); TS&S revenue $404 million (+2%)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Deb McCann, Q2 segments (constant currency): Digital Workplace Solutions $142 million (-1.1%), gross margin 10.8% vs 16.9% on hardware mix, lower volumes and transition costs of a Q1 win deploying Agentic Service Desk across thousands of restaurant locations; Cloud, Applications & Infrastructure Solutions $184 million (-3.2%), gross margin 25% (+420 basis points); Enterprise Computing Solutions $126 million (-13.2%), gross margin 44.8% vs 53.5%; ClearPath revenue $70 million (-22.9%, license renewal timing) with 56.7% gross margin, about 70% expected for the full year; specialized services and next-generation compute grew 3%.
quarterly_data.figure: DWS $142 million; CA&I $184 million; ECS $126 million; ClearPath $70 million (-22.9%); ClearPath gross margin 56.7%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Deb McCann: Q2 gross profit $117 million, 24.8% gross margin vs 26.9%; TS&S gross margin 19.3%, up 170 basis points; non-GAAP operating margin 5.3%; GAAP operating loss of $33 million including a $47.2 million non-cash goodwill impairment (the rest of the Digital Workplace Solutions goodwill, on competitive pressures and pricing); net loss of $95 million ($1.31 per share), adjusted loss of $0.08 per share; adjusted EBITDA $54 million (11.3% margin); year-to-date SG&A $187 million, on track for $10 million-$20 million of full-year cost savings.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 24.8%; TS&S gross margin 19.3% (+170 basis points); non-GAAP operating margin 5.3%; $47.2 million goodwill impairment; adjusted EBITDA $54 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Deb McCann: Q2 total contract value $422 million, including $192 million of new business TCV, up 57% year over year (CEO: up 22% sequentially); year-to-date TCV $696 million including $350 million of new business TCV, up 52%; trailing 12-month book-to-bill 1.2x for total company and TS&S; backlog of $2.8 billion, with a greater share of in-year guided revenue contracted than a year ago. CEO: new business pipeline grew double digits sequentially.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 TCV $422 million; new business TCV $192 million (+57%); backlog $2.8 billion; book-to-bill 1.2x

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Deb McCann, full-year 2026 guidance (reaffirmed after the June Investor Day raise): revenue decline of 5%-3.5%, equating to a reported decline of -2.6% to -1.1% at June 30 FX rates; TS&S constant-currency decline of 6% to 4%; ClearPath revenue $425 million, with average annual ClearPath revenue of approximately $400 million for 2027 and 2028; non-GAAP operating margin 9%-11% (TS&S gross margin +100-200 basis points); free cash flow approximately -$25 million (about $75 million before pension and post-retirement), with approximately $85 million of capital expenditures.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue decline of 5%-3.5% (reported -2.6% to -1.1%); ClearPath $425 million; non-GAAP operating margin 9%-11%; free cash flow approximately -$25 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Deb McCann: Q3 revenue expected at approximately $450 million (about $370 million TS&S and $80 million ClearPath) with non-GAAP operating margin of approximately 4%, implying Q4 ClearPath revenue above $200 million, with key large deals expected to close by year end 'with a high degree of confidence'; Q2 capital expenditures $23 million ($44 million year to date), about half of annual capex being ClearPath solution development; Q2 free cash flow -$49 million; cash $324 million at June 30.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue approximately $450 million; Q3 non-GAAP operating margin approximately 4%; Q2 capex $23 million; Q2 free cash flow -$49 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mike Thomson: in Q2 Unisys moved into production a quantum fraud detection solution at Paysafe, a U.K. online payment platform, developed through an ongoing partnership with the National Quantum Computing Centre (NQCC); Unisys is seeking NQCC third-party validation, which it says would make it one of very few validated quantum production instances. A major ClearPath core operating system release in Q2 eased data integration with third-party AI applications, added an AI developer toolkit and the latest post-quantum cryptography.

CEO Mike Thomson, AI data-center field services: a large OEM engaged Unisys for full-time dedicated resident technicians to support an AI data center build-out and ongoing maintenance, funding their advanced on-site training; a leading global telecom company signed a small expansion for end-to-end deployment and support of Starlink antennas starting in Germany; Unisys is exploring partnerships with system integrators that design and manage data-center build-outs.

CEO Mike Thomson, other Q2 wins: a U.K.-based construction company added Device Subscription Service for 10,000 devices plus Azure services with Unisys as its Microsoft Cloud solution provider; a community college system signed a multi-year infrastructure services scope; a six-year contract with a global travel systems integrator for dedicated on-site engineers maintaining check-in kiosks, bag tag printers and passenger boarding systems in airports across the region, building on momentum in Australia; first Endurance advisory engagement live at a large financial institution; Agentic Service Desk deploying with a second group of clients; first non-IT (HR) use case moving into production.

CEO Mike Thomson: demand accelerated for devices and services as clients face rising hardware costs from memory shortages, driving a broad-based influx of Device Subscription Service demand as IT executives try to lock in pricing; pricing pressure ('AI deflation') is real - roughly $1.7 billion of renewals last year and probably about three-fourths of the way through all renewal cycles by year end; 'I would say, 85% good' at adding new scope to offset it; ClearPath consumption keeps increasing and license durations are steady.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly $1.7 billion of renewals last year; '85% good' at adding scope
